thread:
Mike: quick question — are we comfortable with the current split where hosted gets a simplified control surface and private/dedicated get full configuration knobs? feels like tech debt creeping in :thinking:
Sara: iirc that was intentional to speed hosted onboarding. but we do have a couple of customers asking for parity (esp. routing and traffic shadowing)
Jin: can we enumerate the exact APIs that diverge? my worry is not features but semantic differences (eg: routing fallback behavior)
Linda: +1. From ops' POV the two main differences are: 1) hosted enforces routing policies server-side 2) private/dedicated allow customer-provided routing rules and sidecars
Mike: here are the gaps i've seen: 
- model pinning semantics (hosted implicit fallback to compatible variants)
- per-tenant admission policies (hosted global, private per-vpc)
- audit/event shape (hosted obfuscated ids vs private raw ids)
Sara: that's helpful. tradeoff is complexity vs predictable UX for hosted customers. We also want to avoid accidental config leaks when someone moves from hosted -> private
Jin: propose a small common contract: a "mode-compat" v1 JSON that normalizes the 3 behaviors. simple fields: 
```
{
  "fallback_policy": "strict|compatible|none",
  "routing_scope": "global|tenant|vpc",
  "audit_level": "redacted|full"
}
```
Linda: i like that. but we need to be explicit about semantics. e.g. what does "compatible" mean for fallback? which models count as compatible?
Mike: compatible = same architecture family + identical tokenizer + token-length within X%? (open to better defs)
Sara: we should also add an escape hatch for platform team: `force_raw_mode=true` for migrations
Jin: suggested rollout plan: 1) spec contract and tests 2) wire into hosted as a translation layer (no visible behavior change) 3) add opt-in to private/dedicated to honor fields directly 4) deprecate old knobs after 6 months
Mike: any objections to storing the contract in `controlplane/config/mode_compat/v1` and including unit tests in `infra-tests/compat`?
Linda: fine but add an integration test that validates telemetry shapes (so SRE isn't surprised)
Sara: also ensure we have a migration checklist for customers moving from hosted to private (data retention, audit ids, routing policy diff)
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: created canary job for `mode-compat` spec at 1778010300 — triggered by Jin
Jin: i'll take the canary. will post results here once traffic runs through the translation layer
Mike: thanks all. i'll draft a short RFC and attach the JSON contract + test plan. tagging @Sara to review migration checklist when ready :thumbsup:
